newsitem.title: USA: Thermacell unit price more than triples.
newsitem.headline: Thermacell unit price more than triples.

text.p: Thermacell Technologies Inc units had more than tripled in value by Tuesday from their initial pricing at $4.00 each, helped by the reputation of lead underwriter Monroe Parker, analysts said.
The initial public offering of 1,375,000 units of Thermacell, a manufacturer of insolation material, was priced at $4.00 a unit on Friday. A unit consists of one common share and one warrant.

David Menlow, president of IPO Financial Network Corp in Springfield, N.J., said the current enthusiasm for the units could be attributed to lead underwriter Monroe Parker's history of good aftermarket performance.
"Monroe Parker has a strong history of aftermarket performance for their deals. They are good at making sure the stock goes into strong hands," he said.
Menlow cited Netsmart Technologies Inc and Big City Bagels Inc as two Monroe Parker initial public offerings which opened well above their IPO pricings.
Netsmart priced at $8.00 and opened at $18 and Big City priced at $4 and opened at $9.

Menlow, however, said the value of the company could best be assessed six months from now, when its use of the current infusion of funds coupled with the impact of market fundamentals can act as barometer for the caliber of company on trade.

John Fitzgibbon, editor of IPO Aftermarket, reiterated Menlow's comments, saying Monroe Parker "has a history of initial public offerings skyrocketing in the aftermarket. This is in keeping with their reputation.
Fitzgibbon did not comment on the company's future performance.
The units traded at $15 each in early afternoon trading on Tuesday.
